harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2 and node3 (initial standbys) on CentOS Stream 10, using physical replication slots, scram-sha-256 auth, and firewalld rules opening 5432. Demonstrated failover by stopping node1, promoting node2 via pg_promote() with zero committed-data loss, repointing node3 to stream from node2 on the new timeline, and bringing node1 back online as a standby of node2 (new primary) — all verified with real inserts/counts propagated to all nodes. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time native reboot protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), proving changed boot_id and full data/replication recovery after each restart, ending with node2 still primary and node1/node3 both healthy streaming standbys with 6/6 matching rows.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 16.14 on node1, node2, node3
Configured /etc/hosts, wal_level, max_wal_senders, replication slots, pg_hba.conf on node1 (primary)
Opened firewalld postgresql service on all three nodes (root cause of initial pg_basebackup 'No route to host')
Generated replicator role + password on node1, distributed password to node2/node3 via SSH/scp using cluster keypair (never exposed in tool-call text)
Ran pg_basebackup -R from node1 to node2 and node3, created physical replication slots node2_slot/node3_slot
Verified baseline streaming replication with inserted rows visible on both standbys
Simulated primary loss: stopped postgresql on node1 after confirming standbys had replayed the final committed LSN
Promoted node2 via pg_promote(); verified zero data loss and write availability
Repointed node3 to stream from node2 (new primary), observed timeline switch from 1 to 2
Brought node1 back online as a standby of node2; verified it followed the new timeline with no data loss
Confirmed steady-state replication with a further insert visible on both standbys
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health/data proof on all three nodes
Rebooted node1, node3, then node2 (primary last) one at a time via backgrounded systemctl reboot, polling until reachable
Verified changed boot_id and full PostgreSQL/replication/data recovery after each of the three restarts
Performed final end-to-end write/replication check confirming 6/6 rows on all nodes post-restart

evidence.requirement: Initial streaming replication topology: node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys, data replicated
evidence.summary: node1 configured as primary with WAL streaming to node2/node3 via pg_basebackup; inserted rows on node1 confirmed present on both standbys (pg_is_in_recovery=t).

evidence.requirement: Primary loss simulated without permanent damage; committed data preserved before disruption
evidence.summary: Final pre-failover row committed on node1 (LSN 0/40645B8); confirmed both standbys had already replayed past that LSN (0/40645F0) before node1's postgresql service was stopped.

evidence.requirement: Standby promoted to writable primary without losing committed data
evidence.summary: node2 promoted via pg_promote(), pg_is_in_recovery=f; all 3 pre-failover rows (baseline-row-1, baseline-row-2, pre-failover-final) present, then a new row written successfully proving writability.

evidence.requirement: Surviving standby (node3) re-pointed to the new primary and kept in sync
evidence.summary: node3 reconfigured with primary_conninfo pointing at node2, log shows timeline switch 1->2 and streaming resumption; node3 query shows all 4 rows including the post-failover insert; node2's pg_stat_replication shows node3 streaming.

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary (node1) rejoins as standby of the new primary (node2), no data loss
evidence.summary: node1 restarted with standby.signal and primary_conninfo pointing to node2, logs show timeline 2 adoption; node1 query shows all 4 rows; node2 pg_stat_replication lists both node1 and node3 streaming.

evidence.requirement: Post-recovery steady-state replication verified with fresh write
evidence.summary: New row inserted on node2 (primary) appeared as count=5 on both node1 and node3.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured on every node (boot id + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id bccb87ac(node1)/06339ff3(node2)/d052eb57(node3) plus postgresql active status, recovery role, and row counts before any restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned pre-disconnect, boot identity changed, service/data/membership recovered
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acked before disconnect; node became unreachable then reachable; boot_id changed bccb87ac->c5eae19e; postgresql active, standby recovered with 5/5 rows; node2 shows node1 streaming again.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement returned pre-disconnect, boot identity changed, service/data/membership recovered
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acked before disconnect; boot_id changed d052eb57->888e9aaf; postgresql active, standby recovered with 5/5 rows; node2 shows node3 streaming again.

evidence.requirement: node2 (primary) restart: acknowledgement returned pre-disconnect, boot identity changed, primary role/data/replication recovered, quorum preserved throughout (both standbys stayed up)
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acked before disconnect while node1/node3 remained up as standbys; boot_id changed 06339ff3->130d3c6e; node2 resumed as primary (pg_is_in_recovery=f) with 5/5 rows and both node1/node3 reconnected as streaming replicas within seconds.

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster health check after all three restarts
evidence.summary: New row inserted on node2 (primary) after all restarts; node1 and node3 both show 6/6 matching row counts, confirming end-to-end replication health post-restart.
